top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) rest on a distinct invention, magic-wavelength trapping that cancels the lattice light shift while keeping many atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime, and the 1e-18 performance has been reproduced and intercompared by independent laboratories with several species. The two-name allocation maps onto the idea and its decisive realisation, with the cleanest attribution available; the citation should stress neutral-atom lattice trapping so it stays distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-trapped-system prizes. Twisted bilayer graphene (P002) is excellent science but is hampered by the unresolved pairing mechanism and the omission of the 2018 first author under the three-name limit, so it ranks second and above no award.
recusal_note: Professional connections to Anne L'Huillier, the Lund attosecond group and Ursula Keller's ETH group, plus general atomic-physics expertise in precision spectroscopy; none to Katori or Ye is apparent from the profile, so no recusal clearly required.
